summary: Configured node1 (OpenWrt) as router/services host for the private 10.100.169.0/24 network shared with node2 and node3: gave it a fixed static address (10.100.169.10), enabled its dnsmasq DHCP server for the network, and added a firewall rule rejecting inbound TCP/23 from the lan zone. Verified all settings survive and continue serving live traffic after restarting node1, then completed the mandatory restart-and-recovery protocol on all three managed nodes with changed-boot-id proof and post-restart functional verification.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline network config on node1/node2/node3 (flat DHCP-addressed 10.100.169.0/24, node1 running OpenWrt 25.12.2)
Set network.lan.proto=static, ipaddr=10.100.169.10, netmask=255.255.255.0, gateway=10.100.169.1 on node1; committed and reloaded network

Enabled dhcp.lan.dhcpv4=server (start=100, limit=150, leasetime=12h); discovered dnsmasq's built-in 'already running DHCP-server' self-protection blocking it (platform DHCP already present on segment) and set dhcp.lan.force=1 to override, then restarted dnsmasq
Added firewall rule 'Refuse-Telnet-LAN' (src=lan, proto=tcp, dest_port=23, target=REJECT); committed and reloaded firewall
Verified DHCP server listening on udp/67 and actively answering real DHCPDISCOVER/DHCPREQUEST broadcasts from node2 and node3 MACs via dnsmasq-dhcp logs
Verified telnet (tcp/23) refused from node2/node3 to node1 while tcp/80 remains reachable (proves selective REJECT)
Captured pre-restart boot_id/uptime and health baselines for all three nodes

Restarted node1, node2, node3 sequentially one at a time via native 'reboot' (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect), polled each until exec access returned, confirmed changed boot_id for each

Post-restart on node1: reverified static IP, DHCP server config/listening/force flag, and firewall rule all persisted with zero uncommitted uci changes, dnsmasq and network services running, and DHCP server again live-answering requests
Post-restart on node2 and node3: reverified network connectivity, DHCP-obtained addresses, and that node1's telnet-block/other-ports-open behavior still functioned correctly against them

evidence.requirement: node1 has a fixed address of its own on the shared network
evidence.summary: network.lan.proto set to static with ipaddr 10.100.169.10; confirmed via ubus interface status and ip addr both before and after node1's restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 runs a DHCP service for node2 and node3
evidence.summary: dnsmasq DHCP server enabled (forced past platform-DHCP self-protection), listening on udp/67, and shown in dnsmasq-dhcp logs actively processing DHCPDISCOVER/DHCPREQUEST from node2 and node3 MAC addresses both before and after node1's restart.

evidence.requirement: rule refusing TCP port 23 from that network
evidence.summary: Firewall rule 'Refuse-Telnet-LAN' committed and confirmed present in nft ruleset; live nc tests from node2 and node3 show tcp/23 refused (exit 1) while tcp/80 remains open (exit 0), both before and after all node restarts.

evidence.requirement: settings still in place and serving traffic after node1 restart
evidence.summary: After node1's reboot: uci changes empty (fully committed), static IP/DHCP-server config/firewall rule all intact, dnsmasq and network services running, live DHCP protocol exchanges and telnet-block/http-open tests from node2/node3 all pass.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart with changed boot identity and recovery
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id 2dbf0f75... and health; issued backgrounded reboot (ack returned, then connection timed out confirming disconnect); polled until exec returned with new boot_id 9d3fa534... and uptime reset to ~24s; verified recovered config/services.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart with changed boot identity and recovery
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id f3c5ecf3...; issued reboot (connection reset confirming disconnect); polled until exec returned with new boot_id 2590b37b... and uptime reset to ~14s; verified network connectivity and node1 firewall/DHCP interaction restored.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart with changed boot identity and recovery
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id 095137f5...; issued reboot (connection reset confirming disconnect); polled until exec returned with new boot_id 352dcc0c... and uptime reset to ~18s; verified network connectivity and node1 firewall/DHCP interaction restored.
